corrected_fact: The Bihar SIR order of 24.06.2025 required an additional Declaration Form (Annexure D) with Form 6 from anyone applying as a new elector, and with Form 8 from anyone shifting into Bihar from another state.
evidence: 15. Further, in case of application for registration as a new elector or for shifting from outside the state of Bihar, it is also directed that henceforth, alongwith Form 6/Form 8, an additional Declaration Form (Annexure D) shall also be required to be filled by the applicant to support the declaration made therein. [order page 6 of 19, PDF page 9]

corrected_fact: In Annexure D the applicant declared being above 18, ordinarily resident and a citizen, and ticked one birth cohort. Born in India before 01.07.1987 meant a document for self. Born between 01.07.1987 and 02.12.2004 meant a document for self and one for father or mother. Born after 02.12.2004 meant documents for self, father and mother, plus a parent's passport and visa if a parent was not Indian.
evidence: (i) I am above 18 years of age, ordinary resident on the above address, and citizen of India, and (tick any one) I was born in India before 01.07.1987 ... I was born in India between 01.07.1987 and 02.12.2004 ... Provide any document, for Father or Mother ... I was born in India after 02.12.2004 ... for Father ... for Mother ... If any parent is not Indian, provide a copy of his/her valid passport & visa at the time of your birth. [Annexure D, page 18 of 19, PDF page 21]

corrected_fact: Annexure D also covered people born outside India and those who became citizens by registration or naturalisation. It required the applicant to declare no other citizenship and no other enrolment, and warned that a false declaration is punishable under Section 31 of the RP Act 1950.
evidence: I was born outside of India (attach proof of Birth Registration issued by Indian Mission abroad), I have acquired Indian citizenship by Registration/Naturalisation ... (ii) I have not acquired the citizenship of any other country. (iii) I am applying for inclusion in the Electoral Roll and my name is not included in any other Assembly Constituency/ Parliamentary Constituency. (iv) ... is punishable under Section 31 of Representation of the People Act, 1950 [PDF page 21]

corrected_fact: The documents behind Annexure D were an indicative list of 11, self-attested separately for self, father and mother. An extract of the Bihar roll with qualifying date 01.01.2003 counted as sufficient on its own.
evidence: Indicative (not exhaustive) list of documents to be submitted in support of the declaration (separate self attested documents to be submitted for Self, Father and Mother, if mentioned above, except where extract of the Electoral Roll of Bihar with qualifying date 01.01.2003 is used, which will be considered as a sufficient document in itself): 1. ... 11. Any land/house allotment certificate by Government [page 19 of 19, PDF page 22]

corrected_fact: Every Form 6 claim from a new elector had to carry the new Declaration Form, and EROs were to collect it for all pending Form 6 and advance claims for 01.10.2025. Form 8 needed it only for shifting from outside Bihar.
evidence: d. Every claim for inclusion of name in the roll as new elector shall be in Form-6 along with new Declaration Form. Henceforth, all EROs shall also ensure to collect the prescribed Declaration Form in respect of all pending Form 6 and advance claims received in Form 6 w.r.t. 01.10.2025 as the qualifying date. e. ... New Declaration Form shall be submitted alongwith Form-8 for shifting of residence from outside the state of Bihar. [Annexure B paras 5(d)-(e), page 11 of 19, PDF page 14]

corrected_fact: An existing elector who could not submit the enumeration form in time could file Form 6 with the Annexure D declaration for inclusion during the claims and objections period.
evidence: In case any elector is unable to submit their filled in enumeration forms within the specified time, they may file Form 6 alongwith the prescribed Declaration Form (Annexure D) for inclusion during the claims and objections period. [Annexure B para 4(c), page 10 of 19, PDF page 13]
problem: Minor: the guideline says 'may file'. 'Only' is supported by para 13 of the order (no enumeration form, no draft roll entry) but is not in this sentence.

corrected_fact: For Phase II the Commission made a modified Declaration Form (Annexure IV) applicable. It asks for the applicant's or a relative's entry in the last SIR roll and carries three declarations, with no birth-cohort tick boxes on the form itself.
evidence: c. Modified Enumeration Form (Annexure III) and Declaration Form (Annexure IV) shall be applicable for SIR in these States/UTs. [letter of 27.10.2025, para 2(c), page 2 of 3] Annexure IV: Details of the Elector in the Electoral Roll of the last SIR (if applicable) | Details of the Relative ... (i) I have not acquired the citizenship of any other country. (ii) ... (iii) ... Section 31 [PDF page 27]
problem: The letter says the modified form 'shall be applicable'. It does not use the word 'replaced', which is an inference.

corrected_fact: Under Annexure IV the ERO issues a notice when the last-SIR details given are unavailable or do not match the database, and on receiving the notice the applicant provides documents according to the same three birth cohorts.
evidence: ERO will issue notices to those applicants whose previous SIR Electoral Roll(s) details provided in the Declaration Form are either unavailable or do not match the database. Upon receipt of notice, the applicant to provide the documents based upon the following categories: If born in India before 01.07.1987 ... between 01.07.1987 and 02.12.2004 ... after 02.12.2004 ... [Information Sheet for Declaration Form, PDF page 28]
problem: Minor: 'only after a notice' is a fair reading but the sheet does not say 'only'.

corrected_fact: The Phase II document list keeps the 11 documents and adds Aadhaar, under the letter of 09.09.2025, as item 12 and an extract of the Bihar SIR roll of 01.07.2025 as item 13.
evidence: 12. For Aadhaar, the Commission's directions issued vide letter No. 23/2025-ERS/Vol.II dated 09.09.2025 (Annexure II) shall apply. 13. Extract of the electoral roll of Bihar SIR with reference to 01.07.2025. [PDF page 28]

corrected_fact: The Phase III letter of 14.05.2026 applies the same modified Declaration Form (Annexure IV) with Form 6, and with Form 8 for shifting from outside the state. Its operative declarations are worded as in Phase II.
evidence: c. Modified Enumeration Form (Annexure III) and Declaration Form (Annexure IV) shall be applicable for SIR in these States/UTs. [PDF page 2] Annexure-IV Declaration Form (To be submitted along with Form 6/Form 8 for enrolment as a new Elector/shifting from outside the state) ... (i) I have not acquired the citizenship of any other country. (ii) I am applying for inclusion in the Electoral Roll through Form 6 ... Or I am applying for inclusion in the Electoral Roll through Form 8 on shifting. [PDF page 27]

corrected_fact: The Phase III document list has 12 items. The Bihar SIR roll extract (item 13 in Phase II) is not in it, and item 10 reads Family Register maintained by government officials under any statute or administrative regulation, where Phase II said prepared by State or local authorities.
evidence: Phase III, PDF page 28: 10. Family Register maintained by Govt. officials under any Statute/Administrative Regulation 11. Any land/house allotment certificate by the Government 12. For Aadhaar ... *** . Phase II (CEO Kerala), PDF page 28: 10. Family Register, prepared by State/Local authorities. ... 13. Extract of the electoral roll of Bihar SIR with reference to 01.07.2025.

corrected_fact: In Phase III a person may link to their own or a relative's entry in the last intensive revision of the state concerned. For states already revised, Annexure V lists both the old revision and the SIR qualifying date, so the Bihar SIR roll of 01.07.2025 and the Phase II rolls of 01.01.2026 count as last-revision rolls.
evidence: e. Any person can link himself/herself with his/her or relative's entries in electoral rolls of the relevant last intensive revisions of the respective States/UTs, as mentioned in Annexure V. [PDF page 2] B- Last SIR qualifying date for Other States/UTs ... 3 Bihar 01.01.2003 & 01.07.2025 ... 17 West Bengal 01.01.2002 & 01.01.2026 [PDF page 29]

corrected_fact: Booth Level Agents of recognised parties were allowed to file applications in bulk, up to 50 forms a day to the BLO before the draft roll and 10 a day after it, with a list and an undertaking that they had personally verified each one.
evidence: iii. With a view to ensure more involvement of political parties, the Commission has allowed BLAs of recognized political parties to file applications in bulk, subject to the condition that a BLA shall not submit more than 50 Forms/day to BLO before the Draft Publication, and 10 Forms/day thereafter. iv. BLA will submit a list of application forms with an undertaking that he has personally verified the particulars of the application forms and is satisfied that they are correct. [Annexure B para 9(d), page 13 of 19, PDF page 16]

corrected_fact: After meeting party representatives, the Commission said electors who missed the enumeration deadline could apply in Form 6 with a declaration form during claims and objections, and that BLAs could keep submitting up to 10 forms a day after the draft.
evidence: Electors who miss the initial deadline can still apply during the claims and objections period using Form 6 along with a declaration form. BLAs can continue to submit up to 10 forms per day even after the Draft Roll is published. [ECI/PN/240/2025, 03.07.2025, compilation page 46]

corrected_fact: At the final roll the Commission said anyone eligible could still apply for inclusion up to ten days before the last date for nominations.
evidence: If any eligible person still wishes to apply for inclusion of their name in Electoral Roll, they can submit an application up to ten days before last date for filing nominations for election. [PIB 2173316, 30 Sep 2025]

corrected_fact: BLOs were told to carry at least 30 blank Form 6 with blank Annexure IV declarations during house to house enumeration, and EROs to invite advance applications for 1 April, 1 July and 1 October 2026.
evidence: g. During House to House Enumeration, BLO to carry at least 30 blank Form 6 along with blank Declaration Forms (Annexure IV) ... h. ERO shall also invite advance applications for subsequent qualifying dates i.e. 1st April, 1st July & 1st October, 2026 while publishing notice for draft publication in Form-5. [letter of 27.10.2025, page 2 of 3]

corrected_fact: The Phase III letter repeats the 30 blank Form 6 with declarations for BLOs and asks EROs to invite advance applications for the later qualifying dates of the year. It annexes the 24.06.2025 order and guidelines, which include the BLA limit of 50 forms a day before the draft and 10 after, and its list of changes does not touch that limit.
evidence: g. During House to House Enumeration, BLO to carry at least 30 blank Form 6 along with blank Declaration Forms (Annexure IV) ... h. ERO shall also invite advance applications for subsequent qualifying dates of the year ... [PDF page 2]; 2. The Commission has decided to conduct the SIR based on the order and guidelines issued on 24.06.2025, subject to the following additions/modifications [PDF page 1]; guidelines para 9(d)(iii) [PDF page 16].
problem: 'Unchanged' overstates. The letter applies the 24.06.2025 guidelines 'subject to the following additions/modifications'. None of the listed modifications concerns the BLA limit, but the guidelines as a whole are not unchanged.

corrected_fact: Announcing Phase III enumeration in Odisha, Mizoram, Sikkim and Manipur, the Commission said electors who could not submit enumeration forms by 28.06.2026 may apply through Form 6 with the prescribed Declaration Form, and that BLAs may collect up to 50 forms a day from the public before the draft.
evidence: Electors who are unable to submit their Enumeration Forms by 28.06.2026 may apply through Form 6 along with the prescribed Declaration Form during the claims and objections period. ... the Commission has allowed Booth Level Agents (BLAs) of recognized political parties to collect from the public, up to 50 Forms/day and hand it over to the BLO before the Draft Publication. [PIB 2267217, 31 May 2026]

corrected_fact: At the CEO Meghalaya's meeting with parties, it was stated that EROs had been told to collect the prescribed Declaration Form for all pending Form 6 applications and advance claims for the qualifying date of 1 October 2026.
evidence: The meeting was also informed that all Electoral Registration Officers shall invite advance applications in Form 6 for the subsequent qualifying date of 1st October, 2026 ... EROs have also been instructed to collect the prescribed Declaration Form in respect of all pending Form 6 applications and advance claims received with reference to the qualifying date of 1st October, 2026. [PIB Shillong 2294476, 04 Aug 2026]

corrected_fact: After its meeting of 26.09.2026 the Commission said the declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR had been upheld by the Supreme Court, and that outside the SIR period the forms of the Registration of Electors Rules 1960 will be used.
evidence: The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court. For non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used. [PIB 2315309, 26 Sep 2026, third item]
problem: 'Stays with Form 6 during SIR' is an inference. What the release states is the Commission's claim that the Supreme Court upheld the declaration. That claim is the Commission's, and the judgment of 27.05.2026 names Annexure D only once (para 45 f, describing the order) and upholds 'the documentation regime' without naming the declaration (see rows 40 and 41).

corrected_fact: The Form 6 PDF served on the Voters' Service Portal is the Rules form. It cites Rules 13(1) and 26, lists date-of-birth and residence documents, and carries a five-part declaration with no birth cohorts and no parents' documents.
evidence: (See Rules 13(1) and (26) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960) ... DECLARATION I HEREBY DECLARE that to the best of my knowledge and belief- (i) I am a citizen of India and place of my birth is ... (v) I am aware that ... Section 31 [Form_6_English.pdf, 2 pages, modDate 2025-10-28]

corrected_fact: The Bihar order barred EROs from deleting any entry from the draft roll without an inquiry and a fair and reasonable opportunity to the person concerned, with appeals to the District Magistrate and then the CEO.
evidence: 14. The ERO/AERO shall not delete any entry from the draft roll without conducting an inquiry and giving a fair and reasonable opportunity to the persons concerned ... appeal to the District Magistrate under Section 24(a) ... second appeal ... before the Chief Electoral Officer within 30 days of the DM's order [page 6 of 19, PDF page 9]

corrected_fact: EROs had to list claims and objections in Forms 9, 10, 11, 11A and 11B, show them on a notice board every working day, put them on the CEO website so citizens could object, and give them to parties weekly. CEOs were to post all Forms 6, 6A, 7 and 8 received on their website day to day.
evidence: a. ERO shall prepare lists of claims and objections in Form 9, 10, 11 and 11A and 11B and exhibit one copy of such lists on a notice board in his office on every working day. b. The list of all claims and objections received should also be put up on the website of the CEO so that citizens are able to see the list and lodge objections ... d. ERO to share the list of claims and objections with the political parties on a weekly basis. [PDF page 14]; v. Computerization and posting of all application forms received in Forms 6, 6A, 7, 8 on the website of the CEO on a day to day basis. [PDF page 15]

corrected_fact: Deletions and corrections of entries are completely barred after the tenth day of the announcement of the election programme, so Form 7 and Form 8 applications other than shifting that arrive after the election is announced are to be disposed of after the election.
evidence: b. There is a complete restriction on deletion of names & corrections in particulars of electors after 10th day of the announcement of election programme, therefore all Form-7 and Form-8 (other than shifting) received after the announcement of election shall be disposed of after the election is over. [Annexure B para 12(b), page 15 of 19, PDF page 18]
problem: The bar is 'after 10th day of the announcement', not 'from the tenth day', and it covers corrections as well as deletions. Form 8 other than shifting also covers EPIC replacement and PwD marking, not only corrections.

corrected_fact: BLAs could collect Form 6 claims and Form 7 objections from the public and file objections themselves with a prescribed declaration. Generic complaints without the prescribed form or declaration were not counted as claims or objections.
evidence: 1 BLAs appointed by Political parties can collect Claims (Form 6) from public & Objection (Form 7) from public & file objection himself/herself along with prescribed declaration. Generic complaints, without prescribed Forms or declaration are not counted as Claims (Form 6) & Objections (Form 7). [PIB 2162605, footnote 1]

corrected_fact: An elector of the constituency could file a specific objection in Form 7 before 1 Sep 2025. A person who was not an elector of that constituency could also object, with a declaration or oath under Rule 20(3)(b) of the 1960 Rules.
evidence: If any ineligible elector has got included: Any aggrieved elector of that Assembly Constituency can file specific Objection in Form 7 before 1 Sep 2025. ... Any person who is not an Elector of that Assembly Constituency can also file specific objection, along with declaration/oath as per Rule 20(3) (b) of the RER 1960. [PIB 2162605]

corrected_fact: The BLA declaration linked from the ECI bulletin says the information is based on proper verification of the roll part given to the BLA, acknowledges Section 31 of the RP Act 1950, and is signed with the BLA's name and party.
evidence: I hereby declare that the information furnished by me is on the basis of proper verification of the part of the electoral roll given to me and I am aware of the penal provisions of Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 for making false declaration. ... (full signature of BLA) Name in full: Name of the Party: [Link 4, tinyurl.com/ye26vjxs, resolves to Drive folder 'BLA Declaration Sample' holding file 1qyYxQi833sfztnl6po29um-U8CMBzwZ2]

corrected_fact: The Rule 20(3)(b) declaration linked from the ECI bulletin is an oath by a person who is not an elector of the constituency, naming the person, part and serial number, and acknowledging Section 31 of the RP Act and Section 227 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Samhita.
evidence: Name of person(s) ... Part No. ... Serial No ... 2. I am aware that making a false declaration ... is punishable under Section 31 of the RP Act, 1950. 3. ... punishable under Sections 227 of the Bhartiya Nyaya Samhita, 2023. 4. I further declare that, although I am not an elector of the said constituency, I have personal knowledge relevant to this case and am making this statement voluntarily. [Link 5, tinyurl.com/bt2dred2, Drive folder holding file 1Pn_sS9KuhM7na8F8t1T4dXjrqdNxnI_m]

corrected_fact: The Form 7 PDF on the Voters' Service Portal lets an applicant seek deletion of another person on any one of five grounds, including not an Indian citizen, under a declaration citing Section 31 of the RP Act 1950. The form itself sets no limit on the number of objections.
evidence: (i) I request to delete name of the person mentioned below already included in the current roll due to any one of the following reasons:- (tick any one) Death Under Age Absent / Permanently shifted Already enrolled Not Indian Citizen ... DECLARATION ... punishable under Section 31 [Form_7_English.pdf, 1 page, modDate 2025-10-28]

corrected_fact: By 10 AM on the last day, parties' BLAs had filed 25 claims for inclusion and 119 for exclusion. Electors had filed 36,475 for inclusion and 2,17,049 for exclusion, and 16,56,886 Form 6 had come from new electors aged 18 or above. The bulletin keeps new electors' Form 6 separate from claims to restore names.
evidence: A ... Total | 1,60,813 | 25 | 119 | 0; C Claims & Objections received directly from Electors ... 36,475 | 2,17,049 | 40,630; D Forms received from New electors on attaining 18 years of age or above (Including forty five forms received from BLAs) Form6/Form 6 + Declaration Received 16,56,886 Disposal after 7 days 91,462 [PIB 2162605]

corrected_fact: The Commission put the electors added after the draft at 21.53 lakh, labelled Form 6, and the ineligible electors removed from the draft at 3.66 lakh, rounded to lakh.
evidence: Ineligible Electors removed from draft list | 3.66 lakhs | Eligible Electors added in draft list (Form 6) | 21.53 lakhs ... Figures are rounded to nearest digit of Lakhs [PIB 2173316]

corrected_fact: 24,949 claims and objections in Forms 6, 7, 8 and 6A were filed against the draft between 16.12.2025 and 19.01.2026, and forms pending from before the draft were processed with them. From all these forms 12,166 electors were added and 3,812 deleted. Separately, 35,780 electors were marked ineligible after the unmapped and logical discrepancy cases were decided, making 39,592 deletions in all.
evidence: Out of all of the above forms, total 12,166 electors were added and 3,812 electors were deleted. Further, 35780 electors were marked as ineligible after deciding cases under category unmapped and Logical Discrepancies. [page 2] ... The total form 6 admitted during Special Intensive Revision are 12166 and the total voters deleted are 39592. [page 3]
problem: 'Found ineligible at hearings' is not the note's wording. It says they were marked ineligible 'after deciding cases under category unmapped and Logical Discrepancies' after notices and 'hearings/ collecting documents/ BLO Undertakings'.

corrected_fact: 96,985 claims and objections were filed between 05.07.2026 and 04.08.2026 and processed with forms received earlier. 56,871 electors were included and 30,650 deleted from the draft.
evidence: 6. A total of 96,985 numbers of claims and objections filed during the claim and objection period i.e. 05-07-2026 to 04-08-2026, were processed for the final roll. In addition ... all forms received prior to 05-07-2026 were also processed ... [page 2] 7. A total of 56,871 numbers of electors has been included and a total of 30,650 numbers of electors has been deleted from the draft electoral roll. [page 3]
problem: Page 1 has now also been read. The note separately reports 26,362 marked ineligible at hearings (para 5). Since 19,34,399 + 56,871 - 30,650 = 19,60,620, the stated final, the 26,362 appear to be inside the 30,650.

corrected_fact: 18,598 forms were received online and offline between 21.07.2026 and 20.08.2026. 8,803 electors were included and 1,924 deleted from the draft.
evidence: 6. Atotal of 18,598 Forms were received via online and offline mode during the period of claims and objections i.e. frorn 21-07-2026 to 20-08-2026. 7. A total of 8,803 numbers of electors have been included, and a total of 1,924 numbers of electors have been deleted from the Draft Electoral Roll. [page 3]
problem: The 1,924 excludes the 28,899 marked ineligible at hearings (para 5). Draft 7,18,046 + 8,803 - 1,924 - 28,899 = 6,96,026, one more than the note's final total of 6,96,025.

corrected_fact: The CEO gives additions of 39,243 and deletions of 32,280 against the draft, after Forms 6, 7 and 8 were received and disposed of from 4 July to 2 September 2026, but no count of forms received.
evidence: Electoral Registration Officers and Asst Electoral Registration Officers received and disposed claims and objections (Forms 6, 7 and 8) from 4th July to 2nd September, 2026. ... against the Draft Roll of 8,28,906 electors, a total of 39,243 electors (4.73%) were added and 32,280 electors (3.89%) were deleted [para 3]

corrected_fact: The Court recorded that the Commission had agreed, as an interim measure, that the public notice would expressly say people left off the draft may submit claims with a copy of their Aadhaar card.
evidence: 3. On instructions, it has been agreed that the Election Commission of India, as an interim measure, will take the following additional steps: ... (vii) In the public notice, it shall also be expressly mentioned that the aggrieved persons may submit their claims along with a copy of their Aadhar Card. [order of 14.08.2025, pages 6-8]
problem: The order records the Commission's agreement to take these steps. It does not phrase them as a direction of the Court. (The judgment of 27.05.2026, para 10.10, later describes it as 'the Court directed', but the order itself is the primary text.)

corrected_fact: According to the judgment of 27.05.2026, the Court on 22.08.2025 directed twelve recognised parties to instruct their BLAs to help voters submit the requisite forms with any of the eleven documents or with Aadhaar.
evidence: 10.11. On 22.08.2025, this Court directed that twelve political parties, comprising six nationally recognised and six state recognised parties, be impleaded ... the aforesaid twelve political parties, acting through their respective Presidents of the Bihar State, shall issue specific instructions to their Booth Level Agents (BLAs) to assist voters ... in submitting the requisite forms along with any of the eleven documents specified in the SIR Notification or with their Aadhaar Card. [page 13]

corrected_fact: According to the judgment, on 01.09.2025 the Commission stated before the Court that claims, objections and corrections could be submitted after the 01.09.2025 deadline and would be considered until the last date of nominations.
evidence: 10.12. On 01.09.2025 ... the Commission took a categorical stand that claims, objections, and corrections could be submitted even after the deadline of 01.09.2025. It was stated that the process of consideration of claims and objections would continue until the last date of nominations [pages 13-14]

corrected_fact: The Court directed the Commission to accept Aadhaar as proof of identity, not citizenship, as the 12th document for inclusion or exclusion in Bihar, while allowing its genuineness to be verified.
evidence: Accordingly, we direct the Election Commission of India and its authorities to accept Aadhar Card as a proof of identity for the purpose of inclusion or exclusion in the revised voter list of the State of Bihar. Aadhaar Card, for this purpose, shall be treated as the 12th document by the Authorities. It is, however, made clear that the authorities shall be entitled to verify the authenticity and genuinity of the Aadhaar Card [page 10]

corrected_fact: For people flagged for logical discrepancies, the Court allowed documents and objections to be submitted through an authorised representative, who can be a BLA. It directed the Commission to give everyone who had not yet submitted claims, documents or objections ten more days from the display of the lists.
evidence: (ii) Persons likely to be affected are permitted to submit their documents/objections through their authorized representative. Such an authorised representative can even be a Booth Level Agent (BLA). ... 5. The Election Commission of India shall issue instructions for providing an additional 10 days' time from the date of displaying the lists in the Panchayat Bhawans/Block Offices to all persons who have not yet submitted their claims, documents, or objections [pages 3-4]

corrected_fact: The judgment records that new voters had to submit Form 6 with the Annexure D declaration, and holds that the Commission keeps a bounded residual authority to set a documentation framework for an SIR, with any departure from the statutory scheme needing a rational nexus to its object.
evidence: f. Any new voter was required to submit Form 6 along with a Declaration Form in Annexure D of the Impugned Order. [para 45, page 58] ... The Commission, therefore, retains a degree of residual authority to formulate an appropriate documentation framework suited to the exigencies of a Special Intensive Revision. Such authority, however, is not unbounded. ... any departure therefrom must be informed by a rational nexus to the object sought to be achieved. [para 152, page 106]

corrected_fact: In its conclusions the Court held that the documentation regime is not arbitrary or contrary to the statutory scheme. It does not name the Annexure D declaration in that holding.
evidence: e) The documentation regime prescribed by the Commission represents a considered exercise of its administrative discretion ... We are, therefore, unable to hold that the impugned documentation framework is arbitrary or violative of the statutory scheme. [para 186(e), page 122]. 'Annexure D' appears once in the judgment, at para 45 f.
